newsitem.title: INDIA: Britain's Wolff Olins targets Indian top firms.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Wolff Olins targets Indian top firms.

text.p: British corporate consultancy group Wolff Olins is planning to set up shop in India as an increasing number of companies face global competition, its chief said on Tuesday.
"India is expanding and it is clear that it will be a major player on the world scene in the next 50 years," chairman Wally Olins told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday.
"It will be very injudicious to ignore India."
He said he would be happy if his company could garner about 1.5 million dollars in the first two or three years of its Indian operations.

Wolff Olins, in the business of formulating ideas, visions and strategies for global corporates, has designed British Telecom's new corporate identity besides projects for companies such as Renault, Volkswagen Audi, Unilever and Kingfisher.
"This is part of the infrastructure of marketing human resource development, anything to do with serious corporate development," Olins told Reuters.
Wolff's annual worldwide income is estimated at US $15 million.
The group is now targeting Indian companies as its clients.
"Clearly, the companies we are aiming for are going to be the bigger companies, the more diverse companies and those which have got major interests outside India," Olins said.
"What we are looking for is to create identities for these organisations which project them effectively in a world context."
Wolff Olins had approached a few Indian companies, he said. He gave no details.
"It is vital for India today to start thinking about these issues because until you start thinking about them, your products will not be successful in world markets," Olins said.
